tools.name: Bonded-Fabric Blade
tools.use: Bonded fabric and fabric with an iron-on backer. An Explore blade, so Cricut says it wears faster in the Venture.

tools.name: Performance Fine-Point Blade
tools.use: Comes installed. Made for the Venture’s speed and force. Light to medium materials like vinyl, iron-on and cardstock.

tools.name: Premium Fine-Point Blade
tools.use: Explore blade. Works in the Venture, but Cricut says it wears out much faster than the Performance blade.

tools.name: Deep-Point Blade
tools.use: Explore blade for thicker materials like chipboard, magnet and stamp material. Wears faster in the Venture.

tools.name: Auto Cut-off Blade
tools.use: Sits in Clamp A and trims Smart Materials to length. Venture only.

tools.name: Scoring Stylus
tools.use: Clamp A. Fold lines for cards and boxes.

tools.name: Foil Transfer Tool
tools.use: Clamp B. Fine, medium and bold tips.

tools.name: Performance Machine Mat
tools.use: The Venture only takes Performance Machine Mats. A pass is one trip through the machine. Replace it when fabric slides while cutting.

tasks.name: Change the needle
tasks.why: Counted by seam sewn, estimated from the bandanas and straps you make, not time at the machine. The first look comes at about 90 medium bandanas’ worth, a cautious start for quilting cotton, and your own checks move it from there. For cotton, a Universal or Quilting 80/12. If a layer is fused or bonded, a Microtex 80/12 goes through cleaner, and the glue dulls needles faster.

tasks.name: Clean lint from the bobbin area
tasks.why: Lint builds up around the bobbin case and feed dogs and causes skipped stitches.

tasks.name: Oil the machine
tasks.why: Only if your manual says to. Many newer machines never need it.

tasks.name: Professional service
tasks.why: A tune-up for timing, tension and a deep clean. Counted in hours sewn, not a fixed yearly date, so a slow month doesn’t bring it forward.

tasks.name: Wipe the rollers and clamps
tasks.why: Fabric fibres and dust build up on the rollers and clamps as mats go through, so this counts mats cut instead of days.

review.tip: Body sewing ran 30 min long on a 20-piece run, the third time in a row. Plan it at 2h 40m, and Medium at $18.50 would keep a run like this at your $25/hr.
Every step landed within a tenth of its plan. The fabric buffer could come down slightly.
Consignment at 40% leaves the least per hour of any run. Pricing Medium at $19 for shops would bring it to about $20/hr.
